declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Whitcombe Reyes LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, supports preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The settlement resulted from multiple rounds of proposals and counterproposals addressing both monetary relief and protections governing distribution, administration, fees, and the release. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were negotiated concurrently; fees were not deferred until after agreement on class relief. This declaration summarizes that process without reproducing confidential mediation communications.

The agreement provides a $26 million class fund and a separate $2 million payment for attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Payments will be automatic monetary refunds, allocated proportionally to disputed renewal charges, without claims forms or any requirement of continued membership. Alternative payment methods, reasonable follow-up, and court-approved redistribution will address unsuccessful payments and residual funds. No residual class funds will revert to Brightline. Reasonable, documented notice and administration expenses will be paid from the class fund under an itemized, court-approved budget capped at $500,000 unless otherwise agreed and approved by the Court following vendor bids. That ceiling is not a verified cost estimate. Brightline’s own legal and internal expenses will not reduce the fund.

There is no clear-sailing provision: Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request. Any fees the Court declines to award will augment the class fund rather than revert to Brightline. Our firm receives a fixed $3.5 million under a foundation-funded engagement regardless of the outcome. Any settlement fee award is payable to the foundation, not our firm, and does not affect our compensation.

The gross class fund represents approximately 40.6% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges. If administration costs reach $500,000, approximately $25.5 million will remain for distribution, before any addition from unawarded fees. Although the case survived dismissal, class certification remains unresolved, recovery at trial is uncertain, and trial is approximately two to three years away. The substantial, automatic, nonreversionary monetary recovery reasonably accounts for those risks and delay. Proportional allocation treats class members according to their disputed charges, and the release is limited to claims arising from the challenged renewals.

Hargrove Lane LLP and Ostrander Bell LLP have filed overlapping actions on behalf of the same proposed class. Approval of a settlement releasing those claims would foreclose their continued prosecution and leave those counsel without a fee from their cases. That circumstance warrants transparent disclosure and scrutiny; priority over competing actions is not itself a reason to approve this settlement.

Based on the recovery, litigation risks, distribution protections, limited release, and independent judicial review of fees, we believe the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate and warrants preliminary approval. Final approval remains subject to the Court’s review of the complete documentation, adequacy of representation, proposed notice and administration arrangements, satisfaction of the applicable Rule 23 requirements, and class members’ opportunity to respond.
